name: Infest a vehicle
summary: A small, cheap, fast and fragile attacker reaches an enemy vehicle and attaches to it: it burrows inside, clings on top or welds itself underneath. Once attached it is protected (untargetable in the purest form, or just hard to hit) and keeps working on the host until it is removed or the host dies. The effect can be damage over time, a slow, a blocked ability, a tracking mark, a timed charge or a full takeover. Removal is deliberately narrow, so the latch starts a visible clock that the victim and their team must beat. The trade-off is heavy exposure on the way in for safety once attached.
counterplay: Kill it on the approach: infesters are fragile, so anti-infantry fire and point defence stop them before they connect.
Keep moving and avoid stalls; a pin (stasis beam or EMP) is the infester's setup tool, so dodging the pin is the first defence.
Remove it with repair: a repair station, repair drones, a repair tool or an engineer-crewed vehicle pulls the infester out.
Use a self-cleanse on a cooldown, such as an electric discharge, smoke or a hold-to-shake-off input.
Get a teammate to shoot the rider off, or to use an ability that clears the hull.
Teleport or make the host invulnerable, which drops or suspends the infester.
Sacrifice or abandon the host: bail out, or destroy your own vehicle to deny a chain jump or a hijack.
Spread vehicles out so a chain jump or contagion can't spread through a group.

other_examples.game: extra:Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2 / Yuri's Revenge
other_examples.note: The original: leaps inside a vehicle, can't be hit while inside, and pops out to dive the next vehicle if its own damage kills the host. One drone per vehicle; an infested construction vehicle can't deploy. Only repair removes it.

sources.title: Terror drone (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.note: A flying scout that clings to the outside of a vehicle or aircraft, slows it and can self-destruct a few seconds later to hurt the host and its neighbours. Unlike the terror drone it can be shot off while attached, and repair drones destroy it.

Waits hidden like a mine, welds itself under the first vehicle that drives over it, halves its speed and reports what it sees. It does no real damage: a tracker, not a killer. Repair removes it; sensors reveal it and EMP destroys it.

other_examples.unit: Hijacker and hero sniper crew kill (GLA)
other_examples.note: A stealthed, unarmed infantry unit that takes over most enemy vehicles on contact; a related hero shot kills a vehicle's crew from range and leaves it empty for anyone to claim. Uncrewed vehicles and loaded transports are immune.

other_examples.game: extra:StarCraft II: Legacy of the Void
other_examples.note: Attaches a parasitic cloud to one enemy aircraft that damages it and every aircraft near it over several seconds, so the victim's best move is to leave its group. Damage values differ between versions.

sources.title: Legacy of the Void beta patch notes, Blizzard

other_examples.note: A tether that takes control of one enemy unit while the caster stays alive and within leash range. Kill the caster or pull the victim out of range to break it.
Spartan heroes take over enemy vehicles; the target is frozen during the takeover, which is cancelled if the Spartan dies. In the sequel an EMP leap pins the target first.

shooter_analogues.note: A pilot climbs onto an enemy Titan and damages it from the back (the sequel turns this into stealing its battery and jumping off). The Titan hears a distinct sound and gets a warning, and can shake the rider off with electric smoke or by getting out. A friendly rider blocks enemy rodeos.

sources.title: The Evolution of Rodeo in Titanfall 2, GDC Vault

shooter_analogues.note: Holding a button next to a vehicle throws the driver out; on tanks the boarder clings on top and punches through the hatch or drops a grenade in. Keep moving, have the gunner shoot boarders, or blow up your own vehicle to deny it.
A dart stuck to an enemy vehicle lets teammates lock on with launchers and shows the vehicle to the team for a while: the tracker variant in player hands.

Small spider robots leap onto players after a high-pitched wind-up and hurt them until removed. The victim holds a key to pull it off or a teammate shoots it off. AI-controlled, but a tested model of the victim's side.

player_translation.summary: A cheap, very fast, fragile pouncer whose skill is the approach. Once latched, the player rides the host and makes choices (drill, sabotage, arm a charge, leap off), while the victim always gets a reaction window and an escape.
as_user: You buy a cheap T1 unit with very low health and a short respawn; losing it on the approach is normal, not a disaster.

The skill is the approach: flank, use cover, wait for a stalled or lone vehicle, or have a teammate pin it first. The pounce is a short committed leap toward the cursor that snaps onto any hull it touches.

Once latched, your camera follows the host and you still have decisions: hold to drill (damage ramps up), sabotage a seat on a multi-seat vehicle (jam the turret, cut the engine, block deploying), or arm a charge and leap off.
If your damage finishes the host, you pop out with a short grace period and can pounce again (chain jumps capped). If something else kills the host, you go down with it.
Against infantry, a pounce should not kill outright as in the RTS; at most it finishes weakened soldiers.
as_target: You know at once: a metallic clang, the hull shakes, a large 'infested' marker on your vehicle and a timer ring showing how long until it is critical.
You always have an answer within a few seconds: a self-cleanse on a cooldown, a repair pad, calling an engineer, or bailing out to deny the kill.
Your own main gun can't hit your hull, but other seats can help, for example with a close-defence zap from the commander seat.
On a multi-seat vehicle every crew member sees which seat is affected ('turret jammed', 'engine damaged') and can coordinate.
teammates: Engineers and repair classes get a clear job: a repair beam on an infested hull pulls the infester out faster than it repairs.
Escort infantry with anti-small-target weapons screen vehicles; spacing vehicles out becomes a team skill.
On the attacking side a pinner (stasis beam or EMP) sets up the pounce, and a transport can drop several infesters at once.
Friendly infantry riding on a vehicle can block enemy latching, which gives infantry a reason to ride with tanks.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse.
Left mouse: pounce toward the cursor, snapping to the nearest hull in a small cone.
Right mouse (optional per variant): a ranged pin beam held on a vehicle.
While latched: hold left mouse to drill, Q to pick a sabotage or arm a charge, Space to leap off.
Victim: hold E to shake off or cleanse on a cooldown; each seat has a bail-out key. Teammates: the repair tool's main fire removes the infester.
feedback: Before the latch: a high-pitched skitter and a visible lunge arc, so alert victims can react.
On the latch: a clang, sparks at the attach point, the hull rocking, and an icon on the host that everyone can see from above.
Victim HUD: an 'infested' banner, a direction marker, a timer ring and per-seat status icons, plus an announcer line.
A minimap ping on the infested vehicle for both teams.
A clear sound for a successful removal, and a pop when the infester is thrown out or dies; a radius ring on the ground for charge or contagion variants.
changes_from_rts: In the RTS the infester is untargetable and only repair removes it. Here the victim also needs a self-cleanse and teammates a mobile removal tool, because a drive back to base feels like a death sentence.
RTS players mass many drones; here one player is one drone, so a single infester must matter on its own while its damage still leaves a readable reaction window.
The RTS drone is passive once inside; a player needs decisions while latched, or it is dull.
Instant infantry kills are fine against computer-controlled squads but frustrating against people; soften or remove them.
Chain jumps must be capped and stacking blocked (one infester per host), so a cheap T1 can't wipe a T3 convoy.
The approach and the attached state must be readable from above: tells, sounds and icons, since the camera can't show the inside of a vehicle.
In a browser game, snapping onto a fast vehicle must be decided by the server with lag compensation, or pounces will feel random.

team_play.notes: Both teams get jobs: attackers combine a pinner, a carrier and the infester; defenders need escorts, a repair class, crews that coordinate and riders that block latching.

notes: Attaching is simple in a top-down game: follow the host's position and show an icon instead of climbing animations.
The state machine has many edge cases: approach, pounce, attached, thrown out, killed with the host, removed, cleansed, teleported, host changes seat or bails out.
Networking a pounce onto a moving vehicle in a browser game needs server authority and lag compensation.
Many systems must respect the latch: repair tools, EMP and freeze effects, deploy and transform locks, teleports, invulnerability.
UI on both sides: the attacker's latched HUD, the victim's banner and seat icons, team markers and the minimap.
An untargetable infester with guaranteed damage and no self-counter leaves the victim no agency; inside versus targetable is the main tuning lever (RA3 changed it between patches).
A cheap T1 that kills T3 vehicles, especially with chain jumps through packed groups.
Stacking several infesters on one host, or a pin-plus-latch loop that locks a vehicle down completely.
Hijack variants hand a cheap unit a whole expensive vehicle.
If only one class can remove infesters, teams without it have no answer; always pair it with a self-cleanse.
A tiny infester on a large vehicle is easy to lose from above, and an inside attachment is invisible without an icon.
Players must be able to tell an infested friendly vehicle from a hijacked one.
Each crew member needs to see which seat is affected, not just falling health.
Whether shooting the infester also hurts the host must be obvious.

variants.name: Gnaw from inside
variants.summary: Steady damage from inside until the host dies or the infester is removed; can't be shot while inside.

variants.name: Anchor
variants.summary: Little or no damage; it slows the host or stops it deploying or transforming, so teammates can catch it.
variants.seen_in: RA3 burst drone, Firestorm limpet drone

variants.name: Parasite tracker
variants.summary: Shows the host to the infester's team or enables lock-on; lasts long or until cleansed.
variants.seen_in: Firestorm limpet drone, Battlefield tracer dart

variants.name: Chain jump
variants.summary: If its own damage kills the host it pops out unharmed and can dive the next vehicle; if anything else kills the host it dies too.

variants.name: Ticking charge
variants.summary: Latches, then detonates after a short fuse, hurting the host and nearby vehicles; the victim gets a window to shake it off or spread out.
variants.seen_in: RA3 burst drone, Halo tank boarding with a grenade

variants.name: Pin then pounce
variants.summary: A ranged pin holds the vehicle first so the latch lands safely; can be split between two teammates.
variants.seen_in: RA3 stasis ray, Halo Wars 2 EMP leap

variants.name: Grab and run
variants.summary: A brief latch that rips a resource out of the host (a battery, a shield) and leaps off; the host chases the thief, and the stolen resource can power up a friendly vehicle.

variants.name: Mine latch
variants.summary: Waits hidden as a mine and latches onto the first vehicle that drives over it; ambush and positioning replace the approach.

variants.name: Contagion
variants.summary: The latched effect also hurts the host's allies nearby, so the victim's best move is to leave its group.

variants.name: Crew eviction
variants.summary: Instead of destroying the vehicle, it throws out or kills the crew and takes the vehicle, or leaves it empty for anyone to claim.

variants.name: Tethered control
variants.summary: Takes control of the host only while the attacker stays alive and within leash range.

adds_strengths.why: While latched it is protected and keeps working until it is removed.

adds_weaknesses.why: It has to reach touching distance, so it is exposed on the way in.

counters.why: Lone or slow vehicles without an escort or a cleanse are its prey.

countered_by.why: Sustained anti-infantry fire stops a fragile infester before it connects.
Repair tools pull the infester out of the host.
It can't latch onto aircraft in flight.

open_questions: Should the infester sit inside the vehicle (untargetable, needs a cleanse or repair) or on top (teammates can shoot it off)?
Should a cheap infester be able to kill a T3 vehicle at all, or only sabotage and mark it?
How long should the victim's reaction window be? This needs playtesting.

shooter_fit.reason: A direct player-versus-player duel with a clear tell, a reaction window and a team rescue; Titanfall's rodeo shows it already works in a shooter.
